title: Precision Profiles: INT8 vs FP8 Console Walkthrough - ClarityHealth
next_steps: Redwood to share INT8/FP8 benchmark spreadsheet and console export link
Customer to run a 48-hour pilot on 2 endpoints and report latency/cost metrics
Schedule security deep-dive with ClarityHealth InfoSec (Daniel + Redwood security lead)
action_items: Maya Cho: email pricing/commit options and Dedicated vs Hosted comparison; due 2025-09-15
Liam Patel: export model profile used in demo + batch/kv cache config as JSON; due 2025-09-13
Arjun Singh: confirm target P95 latency SLA and primary inference use-case (triage vs notes gener); due 2025-09-16
summary: AE/SE led console walkthrough of Redwood's Optimize precision profiles story. Focus: tradeoffs between INT8 and FP8, how profiles appear in the Console, and practical latency vs quality numbers for ClarityHealth workloads. Action items include benchmark data share and pilot setup.
topics: INT8 vs FP8 quality regressions and measurement
Latency and cost impact with batching and KV cache
Console: profile editor, rollouts and monitoring
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Cho: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we got about 45 minutes on the calendar, great to see the team from ClarityHealth. quick round robin?
[00:07] Arjun Singh: arjun here, ml lead. main thing is inference cost and hitting 200ms p95 for our summarization endpoint.
[00:12] Samantha Lee: sam, platform. concerned about autoscales and cache invalidation.
[00:17] Daniel Ortiz: daniel, security, i'll only be on for the first 20 to cover compliance bits.
[00:21] Maya Cho: perfect. we'll do a quick Optimize console walkthrough showing precision profiles — what we call precision profiles in the system — then show a small benchmark comparing INT8 and FP8 on a 7B model, and finish with Qs and next steps.
[00:34] Liam Patel: quick note, i'll be sharing my screen, if you see anything unclear shout. audio might be a bit choppy on my end.
[00:40] [screen share begins]
[01:02] Liam Patel: okay here's the Console, nav to Optimize -> Profiles. you'll see a list of profiles: default, low-latency, cost-saver, and the custom one i prepared for you 'clarity-7b-profile'.
[01:20] Priya Nair: can you open the profile details? curious what knobs are set.
[01:24] Liam Patel: sure. profile view has rows for precision (int8, fp8 full, fp8-trim), batch size targets, kv-cache policy and prefix cache TTL, and also model quantization artifact id. while i open it: note we store the quantized artifact separately so rollbacks are simple.
[01:42] Samantha Lee: when you say fp8-trim, is that like aggressive clipping?
[01:46] Liam Patel: it's a trimmed FP8 mode — we reduce exponent range to avoid outlier activation blow-ups; loses a tiny bit of dynamic range but can be faster on some kernels.
[01:54] [02:00] Arjun Singh: real question: how do you measure "tiny bit" in practice? we can't tolerate hallucination regressions in clinical summarization.
[02:07] Rosa Kim: great question. we capture a rubric of prompt sets — we call them eval tasks — and look at both automatic metrics (rouge/bleu/embedding-sim) and human spot checks. the Console ties profile rollouts to those eval sets so you can see a delta.
[02:24] Maya Cho: we'll demo that now: i have a small benchmark run comparing INT8 and FP8 on your kind of workload.
[02:30] [02:32] Liam Patel: show chart — latency vs quality scatter. on the left axis is p95 latency in ms, on the bottom is cost per 1k tokens, and each point's color indicates delta-embedding-sim score (the higher the better).
[02:45] Arjun Singh: numbers?
[02:47] Liam Patel: FP8 mode (fp8 full) gave us ~170ms p95 at 1.8x cost baseline for the hosted job; INT8 gave ~125ms p95 at 1.0x cost baseline, but embedding-sim delta dropped by 0.04 relative to fp32 baseline. i.e., small but measurable quality regression.
[03:08] Samantha Lee: wait int8 was cheaper and lower latency? how come p95 is lower on int8 here?
[03:12] Liam Patel: sorry, i misspoke — INT8 showed lower cost but slightly *higher* p95 in our run due to additional kernel fallbacks we hit on long sequences. INT8 median was faster but p95 stretched to ~220ms. that's why we often recommend a mixed profile: INT8 for short context, FP8 for long.
[03:32] Daniel Ortiz: does Redwood do per-request precision routing? like route long sequences to fp8 nodes?
[03:37] Rosa Kim: yes, smart routing can be policy-based. you can configure the Console to route by payload length, user tier, or a latency budget. it's one of the rollout knobs.
[03:45] [04:00] Priya Nair: how invasive is switching? are we swapping model binaries or changing runtime flags?
[04:05] Liam Patel: we store quantized artifacts as separate binaries. switching a profile updates routing and sometimes swaps artifacts for the endpoint; we do a canary rollout to validate eval metrics before full rollout.
[04:17] Arjun Singh: can the canary compare token-level divergence or a domain-specific metric?
[04:22] Rosa Kim: yes — you can add custom callbacks. many customers push a clinical metric, e.g., F1 on entity extraction, as a gating metric.
[04:29] [04:40] Samantha Lee: latency vs cost: what levers do we have besides precision? batch, cache?
[04:44] Liam Patel: batch size target, auto-batching window, prefix KV cache TTL and whether to enable prefix sharing across requests. in the console there's a heatmap showing expected p95 vs token throughput per policy.
[04:58] Arjun Singh: show the heatmap for clarity-7b-profile.
[05:02] [05:05] Liam Patel: pulling it up — here. you'll see that with batch size 8 and kv cache enabled, INT8 has a lower median but higher tail due to occasional fallback cost. with FP8 and batch 4, p95 tightens and quality improves a touch.
[05:25] Maya Cho: important note — batch sizes interact with user concurrency; if your front-end has sporadic bursts, large batch sizes can add queueing latency.
[05:33] Priya Nair: our traffic is bursty due to app workflows, so we prefer low p95 even if cost is higher.
[05:38] Arjun Singh: show the actual examples where INT8 degraded.
[05:41] Rosa Kim: i exported a few diffs. here's a pair: FP8 produced "patient reports show improved mobility," INT8 produced "patient shows improved movement," which is fine. but one case with lab value rounding produced a wrong unit in INT8 — rare but unacceptable.
[06:00] Daniel Ortiz: this is exactly the kind of regression we worry about — are audit logs available for rollouts? we need traceability.
[06:05] Liam Patel: yes, Console stores rollout audit events, and we keep input/output hashes for each canary sample. for regulated customers we can enable extended retention and tie to your KMS.
[06:18] Samantha Lee: latency SLOs — can you set enforced SLOs that automatically fallback to a safer profile?
[06:23] Rosa Kim: yes, you can set a fallback policy; if p95 breaches for X minutes, routes automatically switch to the safe profile (often fp8 or fp32).
[06:31] [06:50] Arjun Singh: curious about Dedicated vs Hosted in this context, from a predictability perspective.
[06:54] Maya Cho: Dedicated gives predictable hardware so INT8 kernels and fp8 kernels behave consistently; hosted can be more variable but we still provide capacity and autoscale. for a production clinical workflow we often see customers choose Dedicated for consistent p95.
[07:10] Priya Nair: any concerns with GPU compatibility for FP8? we have a mix of Ampere and Ada at our partner infra.
[07:17] Liam Patel: fp8 performance is best on recent kernels; on older Ampere you may see mixed gains. the Console flags the recommended hardware and precomputes a compatibility score for your artifact.
[07:30] [07:45] Maya Cho: quick demo: i'm going to simulate a canary rollout. starting canary at 5% traffic with the INT8 artifact for short-context requests. note the eval delta panel on the right.
[07:55] [08:10] Liam Patel: you can see the automatic checks — embedding sim delta, token-l-level divergence, and a human-sample queue. ran through 200 synthetic samples, 3 flagged for manual review.
[08:23] Arjun Singh: how do we add our internal test set?
[08:26] Rosa Kim: upload CSV or connect to your S3. we also integrate with common eval frameworks and support a webhook to pull results from your infra.
[08:35] Samantha Lee: on the cost side, what's the delta per 1M tokens for INT8 vs FP8?
[08:40] Liam Patel: in our example cluster, INT8 saved ~18% on compute; FP8 cost was roughly 10% higher than INT8 but gave better quality and more consistent tail latency. numbers depend on batch and cache.
[08:55] Maya Cho: we've put together a small benchmark spreadsheet I'll share — includes token counts, p50/p95, cost, and flagged regressions.
[09:02] [09:10] Priya Nair: any gotchas for stateful streams using KV cache?
[09:14] Rosa Kim: KV cache invalidation strategies matter. if your sessions are long and frequently mutated we recommend per-user cache TTL and conservative prefix sharing. the Console shows cache hit ratio and token savings estimates.
[09:29] Arjun Singh: security: where's data encrypted in transit and at rest?
[09:33] Liam Patel: TLS in transit; at rest we support customer-managed keys in Dedicated and Private. logs with payload hashes only; raw audio/text is optional based on your retention setting.
[09:45] Daniel Ortiz: do you have SOC2 + ISO27001?
[09:48] Maya Cho: yes, and we can share the compliance pack. for Private deployments we integrate with your HSM/KMS.
[09:57] [10:10] Samantha Lee: let's talk about pilot scope — what would a minimal pilot look like?
[10:15] Maya Cho: 2 endpoints (summarization + entity extraction), 48–72 hours of live traffic with Canary precision profiles enabled; Redwood provides the benchmark artifacts and the Console monitoring dashboard.
[10:28] Arjun Singh: can we run the pilot in our VPC or do we need Dedicated?
[10:32] Liam Patel: you can run in Hosted with VPC peering for the pilot, or we can do a short Dedicated trial if you want deterministic hardware.
[10:39] Priya Nair: what's the expected timeline to get a quantized artifact for our model?
[10:42] Rosa Kim: typical quantization and profile tuning is 3–5 business days for a 7B model with your eval set; more extensive sweeps longer.
[10:52] [11:05] Arjun Singh: any telemetry we should expect during pilot?
[11:08] Liam Patel: p50/p95, token cost, cache hit ratio, rollout audit logs, flagged diffs, and webhook for your SLO alerts.
[11:18] Maya Cho: okay looks like we have about 20 minutes left for live Qs and a few manual examples.
[11:25] [11:40] Samantha Lee: one more practical — our app does short prompts mostly. is it fair to say INT8 might be preferable then?
[11:45] Rosa Kim: yes, for short prompts INT8 often gives good cost savings with acceptable quality. but add a gating eval and a fallback to fp8 for flagged samples.
[11:53] Arjun Singh: any automated checks for unit/number changes? that's where danger is.
[11:56] Liam Patel: we have a numeric-stability detector that flags changes beyond threshold; can wire it into a canary gate.
[12:05] [12:20] Maya Cho: wrapping up — we'll share the spreadsheet (benchmarks), profile export, and a draft pilot plan. next step: security call with Daniel and our security lead next week.
[12:33] Daniel Ortiz: good, send compliance docs. i have to drop now.
[12:36] Priya Nair: thanks everyone.
[12:38] Maya Cho: thanks team, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[12:42] [meeting ends]
